modules.title: Signals, orders, fills and the event clock
modules.subtitle: Separate the decision price from the price at which a trade can execute.
modules.objective: Separate the decision price from the price at which a trade can execute.
modules.reading: 30-minute session: 10 minutes of original explanation and primary-source reading, 8 minutes of calculations, and 12 minutes of research notebook or project work. Longer independent experiments and exam time are additional.
modules.content:
## Understand the idea

A signal is an instruction inferred from available information, an order is a request, and a fill changes holdings and cash. A backtest that combines them can accidentally trade at a price used to compute its own decision. Define the event clock explicitly: observe the close, calculate target shares, queue an order, execute at the next observed open, and value holdings at the next close.

The next-open convention removes one obvious timing error but does not model queues, auctions or guaranteed liquidity. Overnight gaps change affordability and realized entry prices. Set whether orders expire, partially fill or remain pending; the teaching project expires unfilled quantities after one open. Record both decision and fill dates so reviewers can reconstruct causality.

$$
\mathrm{cash\ after\ buy}=C-qP_{t+1,\mathrm{open}}(1+c)
$$

## A worked example

A signal at a 100 close requests two shares. The next open is 105 and the per-side cost is 0.1% of notional. The purchase consumes 210.21, not 200.20. A signal on the last close has no next bar and must not receive a fabricated fill.

## Put the idea into practice

Draw a five-event timeline and locate the exact cash mutation. In trades.csv, verify every fill date follows its signal date. In the project tests, change tomorrow's close and ensure today's queued target remains identical.

### Research notebook evidence

Reproduce the worksheet, change the stated assumption, and save your calculation and interpretation with the assignment. Record what information was available, what was estimated, and what would invalidate the conclusion. The browser worksheet stays in cash: its price chart does not backtest this lesson's strategy. Use the downloadable Strategy Lab project for multi-asset simulations, trade ledgers and report exports. All supplied companies, prices and results are fictional teaching cases.

## Go deeper: what the research says

*Research extension · about 3 minutes. This summary is Quanta's own explanation; findings and figures belong to the cited authors and the samples they studied.*

Filling at the next open removes one timing error, but research shows that the decision price and the fill price can sit in very different parts of a return. Glasserman and co-authors report that over the past 30 years nearly all the gains in the U.S. stock market were earned overnight, while average intraday returns were negative or flat. Lou, Polk and Skouras examined 14 trading strategies and found that profits were earned either entirely overnight, for reversal and a variety of momentum strategies, or entirely intraday, typically with opposite signs. A label that runs from one close to the next includes the overnight leg, whereas an order queued after the close fills at the open and never earns it. That implication is our reading of their decomposition.

The open can also be an expensive place to buy. Berkman and co-authors found positive overnight returns followed by reversals during the trading day, driven by opening prices that are high relative to intraday prices. The pattern was concentrated in stocks that had recently attracted retail attention, and for retail traders buying such stocks near the open the extra implicit cost frequently exceeded the effective half spread. A flat 0.1% per side, as in the lesson, would not capture that.

Apply it to the worked example. A signal at a 100 close that fills at 105 has already gapped 5%, because 105 / 100 − 1 = 0.05. A close-to-close label would credit the strategy with that gap, while the purchase actually pays it. As an exercise, split each return in your price file into an overnight part (previous close to open) and an intraday part (open to close). Then rerun the rule once with close-to-close returns and once with next-open-to-close returns. If the edge shrinks sharply, it lived in a period that your fill convention cannot trade.

### Sources for this section

- [Glasserman, Krstovski, Laliberte & Mamaysky (2025) · Does Overnight News Explain Overnight Returns?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.04481) — *arXiv 2507.04481.* Documents that, over three decades, almost all U.S. stock-market gains arrived overnight, and tests news-based explanations.
- [Lou, Polk & Skouras (2019) · A tug of war: Overnight versus intraday expected returns](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfineco.2019.03.011) — *Research paper.* Splits the profits of 14 trading strategies into overnight and intraday components, which often have opposite signs.
- [Berkman, Koch, Tuttle & Zhang (2012) · Paying Attention: Overnight Returns and the Hidden Cost of Buying at the Open](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0022109012000270) — *Research paper.* Shows that opening prices of high-attention stocks are inflated, so buying near the open carries a hidden implicit cost.

modules.title: Experiment manifests and reproducible research
modules.subtitle: Record enough information for another person to reproduce and challenge a run.
modules.objective: Record enough information for another person to reproduce and challenge a run.
modules.reading: 30-minute session: 10 minutes of original explanation and primary-source reading, 8 minutes of calculations, and 12 minutes of research notebook or project work. Longer independent experiments and exam time are additional.
modules.content:
## Understand the idea

An experiment consists of more than a parameter and a terminal return. Record the source revision, input identity, universe definition, calendar, feature availability, signal and execution conventions, fees, sample boundaries and all attempted alternatives. Keep outputs together with the manifest that produced them. A file hash identifies bytes; it does not establish that the provider supplied correct or point-in-time observations.

Separate development, validation and final evaluation. Use development data to debug invariants, validation data to compare the predeclared candidate set, and a final segment for the locked choice. Once inspected, a final segment has been used; calling another run 'out of sample' does not restore independence. Synthetic fixtures are valuable for engineering checks but cannot establish an investment effect.

$$
N_{\mathrm{trials}}=N_{\mathrm{families}}N_{\mathrm{lookbacks}}N_{\mathrm{cost\ settings}}
$$

## A worked example

Three signal families are tested at two lookbacks and two fee assumptions: twelve configurations, even if only one appears in the presentation. An archive with one winner and no rejected runs understates the search. A source hash and input hash let a reviewer rerun that exact archive.

## Put the idea into practice

Run the supplied project into a fresh output directory. Inspect its manifest, experiment ledger and source/input SHA-256 values. Enter any additional local trials in the notebook; the program records its own declared candidates but cannot discover unlogged experiments elsewhere.

### Research notebook evidence

Reproduce the worksheet, change the stated assumption, and save your calculation and interpretation with the assignment. Record what information was available, what was estimated, and what would invalidate the conclusion. The browser worksheet stays in cash: its price chart does not backtest this lesson's strategy. Use the downloadable Strategy Lab project for multi-asset simulations, trade ledgers and report exports. All supplied companies, prices and results are fictional teaching cases.

## Go deeper: what the research says

*Research extension · about 3 minutes. This summary is Quanta's own explanation; findings and figures belong to the cited authors and the samples they studied.*

The lesson's twelve configurations are a trial count, and trial counts have measurable consequences. Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado and Zhu showed that it takes a relatively small number of trials to find a strategy with spuriously high backtested performance. With five years of data they say no more than 45 independent configurations should be tried. On a two-year backtest, seven are enough for the expected best in-sample Sharpe ratio to be 1 while the expected out-of-sample ratio is 0. Their calculation assumes independent trials, and for overlapping variants they suggest a dimension-reduction method such as principal component analysis. My reading is that the two fee settings of one rule will behave almost alike, so the independent count is below twelve, but the full count still belongs in the report.

A manifest answers a different question: can someone else rerun this? Sandve and co-authors' ten rules include keeping track of how every result was produced, archiving the exact versions of external programs, version-controlling custom scripts, and noting the random seeds of any analysis that includes randomness. Henderson and co-authors, working on reinforcement learning, found that reproducing results is seldom straightforward, because non-determinism combined with variance intrinsic to the methods makes reported results hard to interpret. Store package versions and seeds beside the lesson's source and input hashes.

Reproducibility does not guarantee agreement. Menkveld and co-authors let 164 teams test the same hypotheses on the same data. The spread across teams, which they call nonstandard errors, was sizable, though smaller for more reproducible or higher rated research. A manifest cannot make two analysts choose alike; it makes their differences traceable.

Exercise: for your own run, write N = families × lookbacks × cost settings, add every other choice you varied, and print the total beside the headline result. Then rerun in a clean directory and confirm the output hashes match.

### Sources for this section

- [Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado & Zhu (2014) · Pseudo-Mathematics and Financial Charlatanism: The Effects of Backtest Overfitting on Out-of-Sample Performance](https://doi.org/10.1090/noti1105) — *Research paper.* Shows how few independent trials produce a spuriously high Sharpe ratio and relates the number of trials to the backtest length needed.
- [Sandve, Nekrutenko, Taylor & Hovig (2013) · Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285) — *Research paper.* Practical rules for recording provenance, software versions, scripts and random seeds, which map onto an experiment manifest.
- [Menkveld et al. (2024) · Nonstandard Errors](https://doi.org/10.1111/jofi.13337) — *Research paper.* 164 research teams tested the same hypotheses on the same data and reached sizably different estimates, smaller for more reproducible work.
- [Henderson et al. (2017) · Deep Reinforcement Learning that Matters](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.06560) — *arXiv 1709.06560.* Shows how non-determinism and intrinsic variance make reported results hard to reproduce, and urges standardized reporting.

modules.title: Point-in-time fundamentals and filing revisions
modules.subtitle: Join accounts by information availability while preserving original revisions.
modules.objective: Join accounts by information availability while preserving original revisions.
modules.reading: 30-minute session: 10 minutes of original explanation and primary-source reading, 8 minutes of calculations, and 12 minutes of research notebook or project work. Longer independent experiments and exam time are additional.
modules.content:
## Start with a simple picture

A strategy can only act on information that existed at the decision time. Historical databases often include later corrections, changed company lists, or adjusted prices. Trace when each input became available before using it in a signal. This unit explains how to build a usable research dataset while keeping those timing and coverage choices visible.

## Understand the idea

An accounting period end is not the date a researcher learned the result. A usable fundamental row needs the company identity, reporting period, publication or acceptance timestamp, units, share basis and revision identity. An amended filing may describe an old quarter but was unavailable to the original investor. A table containing only today's latest figures can silently rewrite the past.

Choose an as-of policy explicitly. The teaching project takes the latest available reporting period, then its latest available revision, and excludes records first available after the decision. Its date-only fixture conservatively permits a filing from the following session. A real feed needs timezone-aware publication and ingestion timestamps, reconciliation of duplicate facts, and a justified processing delay.

$$
\mathrm{eligible\ filing}:\quad t_{\mathrm{available}}<t_{\mathrm{decision}}
$$

## A worked example

A December-period NCAV of 12 is published on February 10 and amended to 9 on March 15. A February 20 screen can use 12; an April screen uses 9. A January trade can use neither. A newer amendment to an older period should not displace a more recent reporting period without an explicit policy.

## Put the idea into practice

Inspect fundamentals.csv and append a future revision. Run the causality test: earlier orders must remain unchanged. Build a separate audit table showing period end, available date, selected revision and stale-age threshold for each decision.

### Research notebook evidence

Reproduce the worksheet, change the stated assumption, and save your calculation and interpretation with the assignment. Record what information was available, what was estimated, and what would invalidate the conclusion. The browser worksheet stays in cash: its price chart does not backtest this lesson's strategy. Use the downloadable Strategy Lab project for multi-asset simulations, trade ledgers and report exports. All supplied companies, prices and results are fictional teaching cases.

## Go deeper: what the research says

*Research extension · about 3 minutes. This summary is Quanta's own explanation; findings and figures belong to the cited authors and the samples they studied.*

Historical databases get rewritten, and the rewrites are not small. Ljungqvist, Malloy and Marston downloaded the I/B/E/S analyst-recommendation history seven times between 2000 and 2007. Between 6,580 (1.6%) and 97,582 (21.7%) of matched observations differed from one download to the next, the changes were nonrandom, and they altered trading-signal classifications. Those are analyst ratings rather than accounts, but a fundamentals table faces the same mechanism.

For accounting data, Lyle, Siano and Yohn compared Compustat Snapshot, which preserves data as it existed at each point in time, with later versions of the same observations. In their working paper, Compustat's adjustments flipped the sign of reported earnings about 14% of the time and the sign of annual accruals about 8% of the time, and the variation stayed high even after restatement-related adjustments were removed. Even when no company restated, the numbers behind a screen can still move.

Without filing timestamps, researchers fall back on lags. Chen and Zimmermann, rebuilding 319 published predictors in open code, mostly use a six-month lag for annual accounting data and a one-quarter lag for quarterly data, and use the earnings report date in a couple of cases. A lag is a conservative stand-in for a timestamp, and our inference is that it gives up information.

Test that on the lesson's NCAV of 12, published on February 10 and amended to 9 on March 15. February 10 is 41 days after the December 31 period end, while a six-month lag would hold the figure back until June 30, about 140 days later. With an illustrative price of 7, the two-thirds ceiling is 8 on the original figure, so the stock passes a February 20 screen, but 6 after the amendment, so it would fail. For each decision date in your fixture, record which of three policies (timestamp, lag, latest restated) changes the buy list.

### Sources for this section

- [Ljungqvist, Malloy & Marston (2009) · Rewriting History](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1540-6261.2009.01484.x) — *Research paper.* Seven downloads of the I/B/E/S recommendation history show widespread, nonrandom changes that affect back-tests of trading signals.
- [Lyle, Siano & Yohn (2024) · Re-Standardized Financial Statement Data](https://som.yale.edu/sites/default/files/2024-07/Re-Standardized%20Financial%20Statement%20Data.pdf) — *Research paper.* Working paper using Compustat Snapshot to show how standardized fundamentals change over time, including sign flips in earnings and accruals.
- [Chen & Zimmermann (2022) · Open Source Cross-Sectional Asset Pricing](https://doi.org/10.1561/104.00000112) — *Research paper.* Open code for 319 predictors that states its accounting-data availability lags (six months annual, one quarter quarterly).

modules.title: Historical universes, missing prices and corporate actions
modules.subtitle: Distinguish an unavailable observation from a zero return or a surviving company.
modules.objective: Distinguish an unavailable observation from a zero return or a surviving company.
modules.reading: 30-minute session: 10 minutes of original explanation and primary-source reading, 8 minutes of calculations, and 12 minutes of research notebook or project work. Longer independent experiments and exam time are additional.
modules.content:
## Understand the idea

A present-day ticker list is not a historical investment universe. Companies enter, merge, delist or change identifiers. Build membership as of each decision and retain exits, including unfavorable ones. A missing quote may mean a suspension, a vendor outage or a delisting; forward-filling indefinitely manufactures an executable price and hides uncertainty. Decide when marking is allowed and when trading must halt.

Corporate actions require consistent units. A split changes share quantity and per-share price while leaving immediate economic value unchanged. Dividends belong in cash or in a consistent total-return series; applying both double-counts them. Raw prices are useful for execution, while adjusted histories support certain signals, but their relationship must be documented. The supplied fixture deliberately has no corporate actions and rejects incomplete panels rather than inventing fills.

$$
q_{\mathrm{after}}=kq_{\mathrm{before}},\quad P_{\mathrm{after}}=P_{\mathrm{before}}/k
$$

## A worked example

Ten shares at 100 become twenty at 50 after a two-for-one split: value remains 1,000. A price-only calculation reports −50% if quantity is left unchanged. Separately, excluding a delisted company with a −80% return from a two-stock portfolio whose other return is +20% changes the equal-weight result from −30% to +20%.

## Put the idea into practice

Create separate status fields for membership, tradability and mark quality. In a real-data adapter, require an explicit terminal-value policy for delistings and test split/dividend accounting before accepting any performance output.

modules.subtitle: Clean observations without allowing future data to set today's transformation.

modules.content:
## Understand the idea

Cleaning decisions encode economic assumptions. Check currency, scale, sign and denominator before clipping an extreme ratio. A negative earnings denominator is not simply a very cheap positive P/E. A stale balance sheet and a genuine zero have different meanings. Record exclusions and missingness by date and sector so data coverage cannot silently become a predictive signal about survival.

For a cross-sectional rule, ranks can be calculated from the contemporaneously eligible universe because those inputs exist at that decision time. For a fitted ML transformation, estimate clipping, imputation and scaling parameters within each training fold and reuse them on later observations. Handle ties deterministically, and define what happens when every value is equal or a standard deviation is zero. These policies change holdings and belong in the strategy specification.

$$
z_i=(x_i-\mu_{\mathrm{fit}})/\sigma_{\mathrm{fit}}
$$

## A worked example

Three comparable positive earnings yields are 4%, 6% and 8%; a fourth field reads 600 because a vendor expressed basis points as a raw fraction. Clipping 600 without fixing units hides the error. Once corrected to 6%, the tied middle observations require an explicit equal-rank or stable tie policy.

## Put the idea into practice

Write a small data dictionary and a cleaning log. Compare winsorized z-scores with percentile ranks, record membership changes, and test that future outliers cannot alter a prior fitted scaler. The downloadable ranker uses symbol order only to make exact ties reproducible.

modules.content:
## Understand the idea

The prediction target must match the proposed holding period and execution convention. A close-to-close label can measure an information relation, but it is not the return of a next-open trade. Save the feature decision time, entry time, exit time and label end for each observation. A chronological row split alone does not prevent leakage when a training label uses prices from the evaluation period.

Purge training observations whose label intervals overlap the evaluation boundary. If the design has additional information overlap or observations on both sides of a test block, choose and document an appropriate embargo; a fixed gap is not a universal repair. Cross-sectional samples also share dates and market shocks. Keep entire dates together rather than randomly distributing stocks from one date between training and test.

$$
y_t=P_{\mathrm{exit}}/P_{\mathrm{entry}}-1,\qquad t_{\mathrm{label\ end}}<t_{\mathrm{validation\ start}}
$$

## A worked example

A ten-session label made on session 95 ends on 105, while validation begins on 101. That training row overlaps validation and must be removed. A label ending on 100 does not cross that boundary. If the next-open entry is 102 and the exit is 105, the gross trade return is 2.941%, not the 5% implied by a decision close of 100.

## Put the idea into practice

Draw interval endpoints for six rows around the boundary and mark which rows are eligible. Use the ML course for full fitted-model pipelines; this lab focuses on whether the resulting signal can be evaluated as a tradable allocation.

modules.title: The systematic net-net screen
modules.subtitle: Turn net-current-asset value into an auditable screen with quality and liquidity exclusions.
modules.objective: Turn net-current-asset value into an auditable screen with quality and liquidity exclusions.
modules.reading: 30-minute session: 10 minutes of original explanation and primary-source reading, 8 minutes of calculations, and 12 minutes of research notebook or project work. Longer independent experiments and exam time are additional.
modules.content:
## Start with a simple picture

A screening rule narrows a list of companies using measurable conditions. It does not complete the investment analysis. For value and quality strategies, begin by explaining what each accounting measure represents and when it was published. Then follow the path from the screen to an actual holding, including the reasons a seemingly cheap company may remain a poor candidate.

## Understand the idea

A net-net screen compares market price with a conservative balance-sheet claim. Compute current assets less total liabilities and other senior claims, then divide by the contemporaneous diluted share count appropriate to the analysis. Current liabilities alone are insufficient: long-term creditors also stand ahead of equity. The accounting number is a starting estimate, not a promise of realizable liquidation proceeds.

Discount doubtful receivables and inventory, inspect restricted cash, off-balance-sheet obligations, dilution and operating cash burn. A mechanical two-thirds threshold can locate candidates while admitting deteriorating businesses that consume their apparent cushion. Separate the candidate screen, financial quality review and portfolio implementation. This modern systematic exercise extends the analytical discipline of Security Analysis; it does not reproduce the book's text or claim that a synthetic test validates a historical premium.

$$
\mathrm{NCAV/share}=\frac{C+AR+I-L_{\mathrm{total}}-S_{\mathrm{senior}}}{N},\qquad P<\frac23\mathrm{NCAV/share}

modules.content:
## Understand the idea

Quality at a reasonable price combines a valuation preference with evidence about business economics. Define earnings yield, invested-capital return and coverage carefully: recurring earnings, net operating assets and financing costs must refer to compatible periods. Financial companies may require different definitions from industrial companies, and sector composition can dominate a pooled ranking.

A composite is a declared preference rather than an objective truth. Standardize or rank comparable inputs before combining them, specify weights, and inspect each component separately. Apply essential solvency exclusions before ranking instead of allowing exceptional cheapness to compensate for an unacceptable liability profile. Contemporaneous cross-sectional scaling is valid when all inputs and membership are known; temporal transformations learned from data must stay within training folds.

$$
S_i=\sum_{k=1}^{K}a_kz_{ik},\qquad \sum_k a_k=1
$$

## A worked example

Standardized earnings yield 1.2, ROIC 0.6 and coverage −0.3 give an equal-weight score of 0.5. Increasing the value weight to 50% and using 25% each for the others gives 0.675. This is a different preference, not new evidence. A company failing a predeclared coverage floor remains excluded under either score.

## Put the idea into practice

Reproduce both composites and compare within-sector versus pooled ranks. The download ranks eligible fictional firms on earnings yield and ROIC after positive-earnings, coverage and NCAV gates. Its simplified definitions are explicit; add a third component only with a new manifest and validation comparison.

modules.content:
## Understand the idea

A cheap security may stay cheap because value is uncertain, inaccessible or declining. A catalyst is a proposed event that could change cash flows, capital allocation or investor information; it is not a substitute for valuation. State the expected event window, the evidence needed to recognize it and the observation that would invalidate the thesis. Avoid labeling every price increase as confirmation after the fact.

Translate new information into the accounts before changing the portfolio. Inventory write-downs reduce recoverable assets, cash burn shortens the runway, and dilution changes the per-share claim. An event-driven screen needs timestamped event data and realistic reaction delays. A scheduled earnings date alone does not reveal its outcome. Use the news-to-markets course to build an evidence chain from a release to the company and its valuation.

$$
\mathrm{remaining\ asset\ cushion}=\mathrm{NCAV}_0-BT-P
$$

## A worked example

A company has adjusted NCAV of 8 per share and trades at 5.5. Four quarters of 0.5 per-share cash burn reduce the simple asset cushion to 6 before other changes, leaving only 0.5 above price. An expected asset sale is relevant only after considering proceeds, taxes, debt repayment and the probability that it occurs.

## Put the idea into practice

Write a thesis-monitoring table with one confirming event, one disconfirming event and one noninformative price move. Connect your entry to [Financial news to company & stock analysis](/curriculum/news-to-markets) and label any event-based extension as unimplemented until its timestamps and cash effects are tested.

## Understand the idea

A screen does not define a portfolio until entry, exit, weighting, rebalance and missing-data policies are specified. A monthly value screen may hold companies between publications, while a daily rerank may create turnover with little new accounting information. Distinguish an eligibility exit from a small rank change and measure how each contributes to trading.

Write a waterfall from the historical universe to usable filings, valid denominators, financial gates, ranked candidates and final constrained holdings. A strategy holding only one name after filters should not silently invest all capital if its mandate caps single-name exposure. Retain cash when too few candidates qualify. Compare the full rule against equal-weight eligible stocks and against simpler value-only and quality-only variants with matching timing and costs.

$$
w_i=\min(1/N_{\mathrm{selected}},w_{\max}),\qquad w_{\mathrm{cash}}=1-\sum_iw_i
$$

## A worked example

Six stocks enter the universe; one lacks available accounts, one fails coverage, and one fails the NCAV gate. Three candidates remain. A two-name portfolio with a 40% single-name cap invests at most 80%, leaving 20% in cash. If only one qualifies, the same cap leaves 60% cash rather than creating a new concentration rule.

modules.title: Time-series trend following
modules.subtitle: Build a causal directional trend rule and identify its regime-dependent losses.
modules.objective: Build a causal directional trend rule and identify its regime-dependent losses.
modules.reading: 30-minute session: 10 minutes of original explanation and primary-source reading, 8 minutes of calculations, and 12 minutes of research notebook or project work. Longer independent experiments and exam time are additional.
modules.content:
## Start with a simple picture

Trend and momentum strategies use past price behavior to form a rule. The timing and measurement choices determine what that rule actually does. Start with one asset and one decision date, calculate the signal by hand, and identify the earliest possible trade. Then compare how ranking assets, skipping recent periods, and rebalancing change the resulting portfolio.

## Understand the idea

A time-series trend rule compares an asset with its own history. Examples include price above a moving average or positive trailing return. These are hypotheses about persistence, not valuation estimates. Specify whether the latest completed close is included, how the warm-up period works, how often the rule updates and whether the allocation is long/cash or allows short exposure.

The rule can lose repeatedly in a sideways market when small reversals trigger entries and exits. A lagged indicator may also exit well after a sudden gap. Parameter choice changes the trade-off between responsiveness and turnover; there is no universally best lookback. Evaluate performance across windows and regimes under the same execution convention, and compare with an always-invested baseline so cash exposure is visible.

$$
s_t=\mathbf{1}\{P_t>L^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{L-1}P_{t-j}\}
$$

## A worked example

Completed closes of 98, 100, 101 and 105 have a four-close mean of 101. The 105 close is above that mean and queues a long instruction for the next open. If the next open gaps to 110, the strategy does not obtain the earlier 105 close. A close equal to the average remains cash under a strictly-greater rule.

## Put the idea into practice

Reproduce the moving average and list signals for a rising path and an alternating path. Compare entry counts under two windows before comparing profits. The project implements cross-sectional momentum; a time-series filter is a separate extension with its own tests.

## Understand the idea

Cross-sectional momentum compares assets with each other, while time-series momentum asks whether an asset's own trailing return is positive. Ranking can select relative winners even when every asset has fallen. Decide whether the mandate holds those winners or adds a positive-return gate; those are different strategies with different market exposures.

Define formation, skip and holding periods in actual timestamps. The French momentum factor uses prior months 2–12; it is a specific long-short research construction, not the same as a small long-only top-two portfolio. A skip period avoids using the most recent segment in the ranking but does not eliminate all reversal, crash or liquidity risk. The supplied daily fixture uses a short declared lookback and one-observation skip to make indexing inspectable, not to replicate a published factor.

$$
M_{i,t}=\frac{P_{i,t-s}}{P_{i,t-s-L}}-1

At decision index 6 with lookback 3 and skip 1, the score uses close[5]/close[2] − 1. Values 110 and 100 give 10%. The current close[6] is not part of that score. Candidate B with 8% ranks below A; a separate positive-score gate determines what happens if both scores are negative.

modules.title: Short-horizon reversal and microstructure effects
modules.subtitle: Distinguish a tradable reversal hypothesis from bid–ask bounce and execution artifacts.
modules.objective: Distinguish a tradable reversal hypothesis from bid–ask bounce and execution artifacts.
modules.reading: 30-minute session: 10 minutes of original explanation and primary-source reading, 8 minutes of calculations, and 12 minutes of research notebook or project work. Longer independent experiments and exam time are additional.
modules.content:
## Understand the idea

A reversal rule expects a recent deviation to move back toward a reference level. It requires a reason: temporary liquidity pressure is different from a permanent earnings shock. A negative return by itself does not establish mispricing. Define the horizon, entry threshold, exit threshold and maximum holding time, and state which information would invalidate the reference level.

At short horizons, a last-trade price can alternate between bid and ask even while the midpoint is unchanged. Apparent negative autocorrelation then comes from measurement and spread crossing rather than an exploitable price pattern. Use quote-aware data when the claim depends on microstructure, include both entry and exit costs, and test slower execution. Daily bars cannot establish queue position or intraday fill probability.

$$
\mathrm{round\ trip\ edge/share}=\mathrm{gross\ edge}-(\mathrm{ask}-\mathrm{bid})-\mathrm{fees/share}
$$

## A worked example

A stable quote has bid 99.9 and ask 100.1. Alternating prints suggest reversals, but buying at the ask and immediately selling at the bid loses 0.2 per share before fees. A supposed 0.15 gross edge cannot cover that 0.2 round-trip spread cost under this simple model.

## Put the idea into practice

Compare a midpoint series and alternating last trades, then subtract a round-trip spread estimate from the proposed edge. Identify what additional data would be required before adapting the strategy to a short-horizon execution engine.

modules.content:
## Understand the idea

A ranking rule can oscillate around a cutoff, replacing nearly identical candidates every rebalance. A buffer or hysteresis rule enters at a stronger threshold and exits only after a weaker threshold is crossed. This can reduce trading but also delays response. It changes the strategy and must be specified before final evaluation. Record whether retained positions can exceed a cap because of price drift and when they are resized.

Inspect a parameter surface rather than only its maximum. A broad region of similar validation results is more encouraging than one isolated spike, but it is still selected evidence. Evaluate costs, turnover, concentration and drawdown across nearby settings. Do not repeatedly inspect the holdout while searching for an attractive plateau. The final choice should follow a declared tie-break, such as lower turnover among candidates meeting the validation requirement.

$$
\mathrm{approximate\ cost\ drag}=c\sum_t\mathrm{traded\ notional}_t/E_t
$$

## A worked example

A top-ten rule with an exit buffer at rank fifteen retains an existing holding at rank twelve but does not admit a new candidate at rank twelve. If modeled traded notional falls from 2.0 to 1.2 times equity, a 20-basis-point per-side proportional cost falls from 0.004 to 0.0024 of equity under a fixed notional approximation.

## Put the idea into practice

Hand-run entry and exit decisions for ranks 9, 12 and 16. Record neighboring lookbacks and their net result, turnover and worst period in the notebook. Label a buffer extension separately from the downloadable engine's unbuffered daily target rule.

modules.content:
## Start with a simple picture

A pairs strategy studies the relationship between two assets and may trade their relative movement. Similar-looking charts do not by themselves establish a reliable relationship. Begin with the economic connection, the statistical assumptions, and the costs of trading both sides. The following lessons show why borrowing, timing, and a broken relationship can matter as much as the initial signal.

## Understand the idea

A pairs hypothesis proposes that a relationship between two assets is sufficiently stable to support a spread trade. Start with an economic connection, then define whether the spread uses price levels, log prices or returns. The units of the hedge coefficient depend on that choice. A coefficient estimated in log prices is not automatically the number of shares to short.

Estimate the hedge ratio and reference distribution from information available before the trade. Define the formation window, re-estimation schedule, entry, exit, stop and maximum holding period. Standardizing a spread makes its deviation interpretable but does not make convergence certain. Hedging notional, market beta and statistical spread exposure are different objectives; identify which one the proposed trade targets.

$$
s_t=A_t-\beta B_t,\qquad z_t=(s_t-\mu_{\mathrm{past}})/\sigma_{\mathrm{past}}
$$

## A worked example

A price-level spread is A − 2B. With A at 108 and B at 50, the spread is 8. A prior mean of 2 and standard deviation of 3 give z = 2. A short-spread trade sells one A and buys two B before sizing; its notionals are 108 short and 100 long, so it is not exactly dollar-neutral.

## Put the idea into practice

Write both share legs and their signs beside every z-score. Compare the same pair under a dollar-neutral hedge and explain why the statistical spread changes. This lesson's worksheet calculates the case; a real two-leg engine is an extension beyond the supplied long-only project.

modules.title: Cointegration, stationarity and half-life diagnostics
modules.subtitle: Use statistical diagnostics as conditional evidence rather than a guarantee of spread stability.
modules.objective: Use statistical diagnostics as conditional evidence rather than a guarantee of spread stability.
modules.reading: 30-minute session: 10 minutes of original explanation and primary-source reading, 8 minutes of calculations, and 12 minutes of research notebook or project work. Longer independent experiments and exam time are additional.
modules.content:
## Understand the idea

High return correlation does not establish that a price-level spread is stationary. Two integrated price series can share short-run movements while their difference wanders. An Engle–Granger cointegration test assesses a particular residual relationship under stated assumptions; its null is no cointegration. Check the integration assumptions, deterministic terms, lag selection and sample size before interpreting the result.

Testing many candidate pairs creates selection bias even when each individual p-value is correctly computed. Reserve later windows to examine persistence and record every pair considered. A discrete AR(1) approximation can summarize local mean-reversion speed when its coefficient lies strictly between zero and one. Coefficients near one imply long, uncertain half-lives; structural changes can invalidate both the estimate and the trading horizon.

$$
h=-\log(2)/\log(\phi),\qquad 0<\phi<1
$$

## A worked example

For a spread deviation following x[t+1] = 0.8x[t] with no new shock, an initial deviation of 10 becomes 5.12 after three steps and 4.096 after four. Its model half-life lies between three and four observations. This conditional decay calculation says nothing about new shocks, changing coefficients or actual execution costs.

## Put the idea into practice

Read the cointegration test's assumptions and write the null in words. Use the [Financial econometrics & factor models](/curriculum/econometrics) for estimation and diagnostics, then design a formation/validation split and a pair-search ledger before ranking p-values.

modules.content:
## Understand the idea

A statistical spread is not an atomic exchange order unless a specific execution mechanism makes it so. One leg may fill while the other is rejected or delayed, leaving directional exposure. Record order identifiers, partial fills, residual hedge, timeout, cancel and unwind policies. An attractive close-to-close spread change cannot reveal whether the two legs were available at those prices.

Short exposure needs borrow availability, a fee convention, collateral and recall handling. Borrow rates and shares available can change during the holding period. Charge commissions and spread on both legs and use gross capital or a clearly stated margin convention when reporting returns. Dividing a long-short profit by near-zero net notional creates a meaningless return denominator.

$$
\Pi_{\mathrm{net}}=\Pi_{\mathrm{gross}}-\sum_{\mathrm{legs}}\mathrm{fees}-N_{\mathrm{short}}r_b d/D
$$

## A worked example

A pair has 10,000 long and 10,000 short. A 0.1% fee on each of four entry/exit legs costs about 40 if notionals stay constant. Borrow at 6% annually on 10,000 for 30/360 of a year adds 50 under the declared simple convention. A 120 gross gain leaves only 30 before spread, impact and financing.

## Put the idea into practice

Write a state table for both filled, long-only filled, short-only filled, rejected borrow and recall. Define a maximum unhedged interval and a cash-reserved unwind action. These are design exercises; the supplied long-only engine does not pretend to simulate short borrow or atomic pair fills.

modules.objective: Decide when new information invalidates a spread and design an auditable pair experiment.
modules.reading: 30-minute session: 10 minutes of original explanation and primary-source reading, 8 minutes of calculations, and 12 minutes of research notebook or project work. Longer independent experiments and exam time are additional.
modules.content:
## Understand the idea

A spread relationship can break after a merger, a capital-structure change, a business divestiture or a persistent shift in input economics. A widening z-score may therefore reflect a new equilibrium rather than a larger bargain. Monitor both statistical behavior and the economic link. Define observation windows and stop rules before looking at the most dramatic historical episode.

Separate a trading stop from model re-estimation. A stop bounds a particular position under imperfect execution; it does not prove the model is wrong or cap loss through every gap. Re-estimation changes the model and needs later validation. Averaging down increases exposure to the same unverified relationship. Record a maximum holding time and borrow/hedge limits even if the original statistical fit was strong.

$$
\mathrm{exit\ reason}\in\{\mathrm{convergence},\mathrm{risk},\mathrm{time},\mathrm{borrow},\mathrm{thesis\ break}\}
$$

## A worked example

A spread enters at z = 2, has a planned exit at 0.5 and a risk exit at 3.5. A structural announcement moves it from 3.2 to 4.2 overnight. The strategy cannot assume execution at 3.5 through the gap; the actual next executable prices determine the loss on both legs.

## Put the idea into practice

Complete a pair research protocol with formation sample, hedge units, diagnostics, entry/exit policy, two-leg costs and a break scenario. Compare it with the single-asset engine contract and list the additional events needed before a pairs extension could be considered implemented.

modules.objective: Turn time-valid predictions into a researchable allocation with a simple baseline.
modules.reading: 30-minute session: 10 minutes of original explanation and primary-source reading, 8 minutes of calculations, and 12 minutes of research notebook or project work. Longer independent experiments and exam time are additional.
modules.content:
## Start with a simple picture

A prediction becomes part of a strategy only after you decide how it changes holdings. A model may rank stocks or estimate a return, but the portfolio also needs sizing, constraints, timing, and costs. In this unit, follow the prediction through those decisions. Evaluate the complete process on later data and compare it with simpler rules.

## Understand the idea

A stock-prediction model is one component in a strategy. Define the observable features, tradable target, training dates, refit schedule, prediction output and rule converting predictions to positions. A lower prediction error does not by itself establish better portfolio returns: ranking, turnover, costs and constraints mediate the economic outcome. Begin with a simple factor rank and a regularized linear model before adding flexible alternatives.

Fit imputation, scaling, feature selection and model parameters within training data. Keep all stocks from a date together and purge overlapping forward labels. A cross-sectional ranking at a decision time can use the available cross-section, but a learned preprocessing pipeline cannot learn from the future test distribution. Record model and feature versions alongside every prediction so an execution audit can identify what was actually used.

$$
\widehat\beta=\arg\min_\beta\{\|y-X\beta\|_2^2+\lambda\|\beta\|_2^2\}
$$

## A worked example

A single-feature ridge fit without an intercept has sum(xy) = 6 and sum(x²) = 4. With penalty 2, the coefficient is 1 rather than the unpenalized 1.5. This arithmetic illustrates shrinkage; choosing the penalty after seeing the holdout would still contaminate evaluation, and the example is not a complete trained stock model.

## Put the idea into practice

Write the prediction-to-position contract and compare a frozen rank baseline. Continue to the [Machine learning for stocks](/curriculum/stock-machine-learning) for fitted pipelines, training and evaluation; return here to audit timing, sizing and after-cost portfolio evidence.

modules.title: Walk-forward model selection and nested validation
modules.subtitle: Separate hyperparameter selection from evaluation of the selected training procedure.
modules.objective: Separate hyperparameter selection from evaluation of the selected training procedure.
modules.reading: 30-minute session: 10 minutes of original explanation and primary-source reading, 8 minutes of calculations, and 12 minutes of research notebook or project work. Longer independent experiments and exam time are additional.
modules.content:
## Understand the idea

A walk-forward experiment repeatedly fits on past information and evaluates on a later block. If hyperparameters are selected within that process, use inner training/validation splits restricted to the outer training history. The outer block then evaluates the whole selection procedure rather than a model chosen with knowledge of that block. Purge label overlaps at every relevant boundary, not just the final split.

Specify expanding versus rolling history, training-window length, retraining frequency and what happens when too little valid data remain. A model can use earlier evaluation observations once they become past data in a later live-like refit, but the original evaluation prediction must remain frozen. Chronology determines admissible information; it does not guarantee stationarity or sufficient effective sample size.

$$

modules.content:
## Understand the idea

A cross-sectional information coefficient measures association between predicted scores and later outcomes at a date. Rank correlation emphasizes ordering rather than return calibration. Compute diagnostics by date and inspect their distribution rather than pooling every stock-date into one impressive number. Observations share market shocks and overlapping labels, so a naive count of rows can overstate independent evidence.

Rank buckets and top-minus-bottom returns help explain the shape of a signal, but a long-short diagnostic is not the same as an implementable long-only portfolio. Compare the actual selected names, turnover, sector exposures and capacity. A weak global rank correlation can coexist with useful tail separation, while a positive correlation can disappear after implementation costs. Keep both the statistical and economic views visible.

$$
\rho_s=1-\frac{6\sum_i d_i^2}{n(n^2-1)}\quad\mathrm{(no\ ties)}
$$

## A worked example

Across three assets, predicted ranks [1,2,3] and realized ranks [2,1,3] have squared rank differences totaling 2. With no ties, Spearman correlation is 1 − 6×2/(3×(3²−1)) = 0.5. This tiny fictional cross-section provides a calculation check, not evidence of a persistent signal.

## Put the idea into practice

Reproduce the rank coefficient, then write a dated diagnostic table with bucket returns, selected-name concentration and traded notional. State how ties are ranked. Link every claimed net return to the engine's holdings and ledger, rather than applying an IC directly to capital.

modules.title: Ablations, negative controls and model failure analysis
modules.subtitle: Test whether added complexity contributes evidence and detect suspiciously good results.
modules.objective: Test whether added complexity contributes evidence and detect suspiciously good results.
modules.reading: 30-minute session: 10 minutes of original explanation and primary-source reading, 8 minutes of calculations, and 12 minutes of research notebook or project work. Longer independent experiments and exam time are additional.
modules.content:
## Understand the idea

An ablation removes or simplifies a component while preserving the surrounding experiment. Compare value-only with value-plus-quality, a fixed rank with a trained model, and the same signal under slower execution. Match sample, costs and constraints so a difference has an interpretable cause. An ablation is another trial; do not report only the one that favors the preferred model.

Negative controls probe the research machinery. Random labels or deliberately uninformative features should not reliably produce exceptional independent predictions. If they do, investigate leakage, selection and evaluation code before celebrating the original signal. Shuffling must respect the question and dependence structure; indiscriminate row shuffling can remove time dependence and create an unrealistically easy null. Controls diagnose problems, but passing them does not prove a real economic advantage.

$$
\Delta_{\mathrm{ablation}}=M(\mathrm{full\ rule})-M(\mathrm{matched\ simpler\ rule})
$$

## A worked example

A baseline has validation net return 4%, an added feature raises it to 4.1%, and doubling modeled costs reduces the new rule to 1%. If the feature also triples turnover, the incremental prediction result may have little implementation value. A random-label run that appears excellent warrants an audit of label timing and the full search count.

## Put the idea into practice

Create an ablation matrix with one changed element per row and retain losses. Use a fixed seed for controls and record their construction. For a failed experiment, write whether the mechanism, data, model, portfolio or execution assumption was challenged.

modules.title: Position sizing, exposure caps and volatility targets
modules.subtitle: Translate a score into bounded exposure while treating risk estimates as uncertain.
modules.objective: Translate a score into bounded exposure while treating risk estimates as uncertain.
modules.reading: 30-minute session: 10 minutes of original explanation and primary-source reading, 8 minutes of calculations, and 12 minutes of research notebook or project work. Longer independent experiments and exam time are additional.
modules.content:
## Start with a simple picture

Several attractive signals can still produce a concentrated or unaffordable portfolio. Portfolio construction decides how much to hold and how the positions interact. Start with a small set of proposed weights, then check cash, exposure limits, and the effect of trading costs. Accounting for the resulting trades lets you verify that the strategy you measured is the one you intended.

## Understand the idea

A signal says which exposure is preferred; sizing determines how much risk reaches the portfolio. Start with equal weights, a single-name cap, a gross exposure limit and a cash rule. Integer shares, lot sizes and next-open gaps mean realized weights differ from target weights. Record requested and filled quantities so a cash constraint cannot silently appear as a better signal.

Volatility targeting scales exposure using a past estimate of risk. Specify the return horizon, estimator, floor, rebalance frequency and leverage cap. A low recent estimate can otherwise produce excessive leverage just before a shock. Volatility is not a complete loss model: gaps, correlation changes and illiquidity remain possible. Use stress scenarios and capital constraints alongside the estimate rather than interpreting a target as a guaranteed realized volatility.

$$
g_t=\min(g_{\max},\sigma_{\mathrm{target}}/\max(\widehat\sigma_t,\sigma_{\min}))
$$

## A worked example

A 10% target divided by a 20% annualized estimate suggests 0.5 times exposure. If the estimate falls to 4%, the raw multiplier is 2.5; a declared 1.2 cap limits it to 1.2. The resulting future volatility can still exceed 10% if conditions change.

## Put the idea into practice

Calculate target and capped exposure, then convert a 40% weight on 10,000 equity at a 103 close into 38 whole shares. Explain how a next-open gap and fees can reduce the actual purchase. The lab uses long-only caps without volatility leverage; targeting is a tested extension assignment.

modules.title: Covariance, diversification and portfolio constraints
modules.subtitle: Evaluate joint exposures rather than treating several strategies as independent bets.
modules.objective: Evaluate joint exposures rather than treating several strategies as independent bets.
modules.reading: 30-minute session: 10 minutes of original explanation and primary-source reading, 8 minutes of calculations, and 12 minutes of research notebook or project work. Longer independent experiments and exam time are additional.
modules.content:
## Understand the idea

Combining strategies changes the portfolio through weights and covariance, not through the number of names alone. Two individually attractive signals may own the same stocks or respond to the same macro factor. Inspect holdings overlap, sector and factor exposures, and correlations of aligned net returns. Correlations estimated in quiet periods may rise during stress, exactly when diversification is most valuable.

A minimum-variance or risk-budget allocation depends on uncertain covariance estimates. Small samples and nearly duplicate strategies can make unconstrained solutions unstable. Compare a simple equal-weight allocation with constrained alternatives, regularize estimates when justified, and report sensitivity. Exposure limits and cash reserves express the mandate; an optimizer should not silently violate them to produce an attractive historical objective.

$$
\sigma_p^2=w_A^2\sigma_A^2+w_B^2\sigma_B^2+2w_Aw_B\rho\sigma_A\sigma_B
$$

## A worked example

Two sleeves each have 20% volatility and receive 50% weights. At correlation zero, portfolio variance is 0.02 and volatility about 14.14%. At correlation one, volatility becomes 20%. Merely labeling the sleeves 'value' and 'AI' does not establish the zero-correlation assumption.

## Put the idea into practice

modules.title: Turnover, transaction costs and strategy capacity
modules.subtitle: State turnover conventions and test whether proposed orders fit plausible liquidity.
modules.objective: State turnover conventions and test whether proposed orders fit plausible liquidity.
modules.reading: 30-minute session: 10 minutes of original explanation and primary-source reading, 8 minutes of calculations, and 12 minutes of research notebook or project work. Longer independent experiments and exam time are additional.
modules.content:
## Understand the idea

Turnover measures trading activity, but conventions differ. The sum of absolute weight changes counts both purchases and sales; half that sum is often called one-way turnover for a fully invested rebalance. Fees assessed per traded notional apply to the full traded amount. Mixing these conventions can understate cost by a factor of two. Keep cash changes and drift assumptions explicit.

Capacity asks whether more capital changes the execution economics. Measure order size relative to an observable liquidity estimate, then consider spread, impact, urgency and participation limits. A fixed fee does not capture market impact, and current-session total volume is unknown at the open. The teaching engine uses a fraction of prior-session volume as a quantity cap; this is a transparent approximation, not a claim about actual opening liquidity.

$$
T_{\mathrm{traded}}=\sum_i|w_i^*-w_i|,\qquad C/E\approx cT_{\mathrm{traded}}
$$

## A worked example

Weights move from [0.6,0.4] to [0.4,0.6]. Absolute changes total 0.4; one-way turnover is 0.2. At 20 basis points per traded notional, approximate fee drag is 0.0008 of equity. A desired 300-share order with a 5% cap on prior volume of 2,000 can fill at most 100 shares under the lab policy.

## Put the idea into practice

Reconcile both turnover conventions, double costs and reduce the participation cap. Compare unfilled quantities and cash across runs. Record that a prior-volume proxy cannot determine the actual order book or spread available at the opening event.

modules.title: Portfolio accounting and independent engine checks
modules.subtitle: Reconcile cash, holdings, fees and wealth with a hand-calculated event ledger.
modules.objective: Reconcile cash, holdings, fees and wealth with a hand-calculated event ledger.
modules.reading: 30-minute session: 10 minutes of original explanation and primary-source reading, 8 minutes of calculations, and 12 minutes of research notebook or project work. Longer independent experiments and exam time are additional.
modules.content:
## Understand the idea

Before interpreting performance, prove that the engine accounts for its own events. Each fill changes shares and cash once, fees are charged once, and wealth equals cash plus marked holdings. Process sells before buys if that is the declared rebalance convention, maintain deterministic allocation when cash is scarce, and record partial fills. A correct signal with incorrect accounting produces an invalid research result.

Use tiny independent fixtures with obvious expected answers: constant prices, an overnight gap, one profitable round trip, one losing round trip, insufficient cash and a final unexecuted signal. Compare event-ledger arithmetic with the wealth path. Tests that simply repeat the implementation's formula are weaker than a separately worked cash ledger. Mark remaining holdings at the end and disclose whether liquidation costs are included.

$$
E_t=C_t+\sum_i q_{i,t}P_{i,t},\qquad \Pi_{\mathrm{net}}=\Pi_{\mathrm{gross}}-\mathrm{fees}
$$

## A worked example

Start with 1,000. Buy two shares at the next open of 100 with a 1% fee: cash becomes 798. Sell both at a later open of 110 with a 1% fee: proceeds are 217.8 and final cash is 1,015.8. Gross gain is 20, fees total 4.2 and net gain is 15.8.

## Put the idea into practice

modules.content:
## Start with a simple picture

The final research stage asks whether the selected strategy deserves further work. Keep the evaluation period separate from the trials used to choose it. Then challenge the result with reasonable changes to assumptions, parameters, and execution conditions. A defensible conclusion explains what passed, what failed, and which parts of the idea remain untested.

## Understand the idea

A research comparison needs a selection protocol, not only a train/test label. Fix the candidate list, development period, validation objective, tie-break and final evaluation window. Use development fixtures to find implementation errors, then select the candidate using validation outcomes only. Freeze the specification before revealing the final segment and record that the segment has now been consumed.

A reset evaluation and a continuous walk-forward simulation answer different questions. The supplied project starts each validation and test account in cash at the preceding decision close, with historical observations available only for indicator warm-up. No earlier holdings are imported. A continuous strategy would carry holdings and accounting state across the boundary; implement and disclose that separately. Short synthetic segments exercise this procedure but cannot provide convincing market evidence.

$$
j^*=\arg\max_j R_{j,\mathrm{validation}},\qquad R_{\mathrm{reported}}=R_{j^*,\mathrm{test}}
$$

## A worked example

Validation net returns for equal-weight, value-quality and momentum are 2%, 3% and 1%. The predeclared highest-return rule selects value-quality. If the later test returns −4%, the result remains −4%; selecting equal-weight after seeing test outcomes would turn that segment into another selection sample.

## Put the idea into practice

Run strategy_lab.py and inspect experiments.json. Confirm the winner depends only on validation rows. Open the selected strategy's test export after writing your prediction in the notebook. The program evaluates only the selected candidate on the final segment; repeated manual trials still need disclosure.

modules.objective: Interpret a selected backtest in light of search effort and dependent observations.

modules.content:
## Understand the idea

The best result among many noisy trials tends to look better than its underlying process. Count families, features, windows, costs, benchmarks and informal revisions, not just the final grid. A nominal p-value or Sharpe estimate for the selected winner does not automatically account for that search. The probability-of-backtest-overfitting literature formalizes aspects of selection; citing it is not the same as implementing its procedure.

Returns also exhibit dependence and changing regimes. A row-wise bootstrap may break serial structure, while a block bootstrap preserves some local dependence under its own stationarity and block-length assumptions. Uncertainty intervals from one selected series remain conditional on selection unless the procedure explicitly models the search. Use descriptive intervals, independent periods and economic reasoning together, and distinguish a failed rejection from proof that no effect exists.

$$
\Pr(\mathrm{at\ least\ one\ false\ positive})=1-(1-\alpha)^m\quad\mathrm{(independent\ nulls)}
$$

## A worked example

If twenty independent null tests each have a 5% false-positive probability, the chance of at least one false positive is 1 − 0.95²⁰, about 64.15%. Real strategy trials are usually dependent, so this is an illustrative independence calculation rather than the exact probability for a research grid.

## Put the idea into practice

Record the complete trial count and identify dependencies among settings. Use the final reporting course's block-uncertainty tool for a descriptive interval, explicitly retaining its selection caveat. Do not label a simple count or bootstrap as a computed PBO estimate.

modules.title: Stress experiments and implementation readiness
modules.subtitle: Challenge a frozen strategy with adverse costs, delays, liquidity and concentration.
modules.objective: Challenge a frozen strategy with adverse costs, delays, liquidity and concentration.
modules.reading: 30-minute session: 10 minutes of original explanation and primary-source reading, 8 minutes of calculations, and 12 minutes of research notebook or project work. Longer independent experiments and exam time are additional.
modules.content:
## Understand the idea

Stress tests ask how the proposed rule behaves when an assumption becomes less favorable. Keep the candidate fixed while increasing costs, tightening a prior-volume participation cap, delaying execution, removing a feature or imposing a concentration shock. Preserve the base input identity when testing one changed assumption so the comparison remains interpretable. A stress is a scenario, not a prediction of its probability.

Separate implementation readiness from expected profitability. Correct accounting, deterministic replay and clean inputs support engineering confidence. Later independent performance, an economic mechanism and robust implementation assumptions support a research argument. Paper execution adds evidence about data freshness, order handling and reconciliation without proving that live fills will match. Set concrete pause conditions such as stale inputs, irreconcilable holdings or an unexplained model-version change.

$$
\mathrm{stress\ impact}=M(\mathrm{fixed\ rule},\mathrm{adverse\ assumption})-M(\mathrm{fixed\ rule},\mathrm{base})
$$

## A worked example

A fixed strategy returns 5% at base costs, 1% at doubled costs and −2% under a tighter liquidity cap. The appropriate conclusion identifies execution sensitivity rather than averaging the three into a guaranteed return. If a replay changes earlier fills after only future data are edited, that is a causality defect requiring repair before any performance claim.

## Put the idea into practice

Run the download's cost and liquidity stress modes on the selected rule, retain every output and label them as post-selection diagnostics. Propose a one-event execution delay as an extension. Use the Python bot or C/HPC track for subsequent operational implementation.

## Understand the idea

The capstone combines the strategy contract, data audit, experiment ledger, selected rule, order and position records, net wealth path, benchmark and limitations. Reproduce the supplied engine's independent fixtures before studying its fictional results. Then complete one predeclared research extension and show what changed, what remained fixed and what evidence challenged the original idea. A careful negative result is a successful research deliverable.

The downloadable engine runs equal-weight, value-quality and momentum portfolios with available filings, next-open fills, fees, whole shares, cash and prior-volume caps. It selects on a validation segment, evaluates the frozen choice on a later synthetic segment, and exports two post-selection stresses. Pairs execution, fitted ML, corporate actions and real market adapters are explicit extension work. Do not describe them as implemented merely because their design appears in the course.

$$
\mathrm{dossier}=\mathrm{specification}+\mathrm{audited\ data}+\mathrm{tested\ execution}+\mathrm{independent\ evaluation}+\mathrm{limitations}
$$

## A worked example

Your engine fixture must finish the two-share round trip at 1,015.8 with 4.2 of fees. The 100-point dossier rubric allocates 20 to hypothesis/data, 25 to timing/accounting, 20 to comparison/selection, 20 to stress/limitations and 15 to reproducibility/communication. Unresolved look-ahead or unreconciled cash requires revision regardless of score.

## Put the idea into practice

Run the archive tests and project, complete research-notebook.md and inspect the exported CSV/JSON files. Send the base test equity.csv and manifest.json to [Algorithm evaluation & results reporting](/curriculum/algorithm-evaluation) for the final report, charts and written decision. Continue operational implementation in [Algorithmic & AI stock bots](/curriculum/stock-bots) or [Algorithmic trading II: C & high-performance computing](/curriculum/c-hpc-trading) with the same research contract.

readingGuide:
An investment idea becomes a strategy only when another person could follow its rules and reach the same decisions. This course takes you through that translation: define the idea, choose data that was available at the time, create a signal, decide what to hold, and record how trades change the portfolio.

For each strategy family, start with the reason it might work and the reason it might fail. Follow the worked calculation, then use the project to inspect individual holdings, trades, and costs. Compare the result with a simple alternative over the same period. A useful research result may be a clear reason to reject an idea; the goal is to reach a conclusion you can explain and reproduce.

32 lessons × 30 minutes = 16 hours of planned study across eight units; exam time is additional. Includes 64 practice questions, eight four-question checkpoints, a 32-question final, a downloadable Python research project and a separately self-assessed capstone.

Original fictional cases teach research methods; they do not establish real-market profitability. The local engine implements equal-weight, value-quality and momentum portfolios.

Pairs and ML receive guided design/calculation labs; their full engines are extension assignments linked to the econometrics and stock-ML courses.
